faq.q: How many quills does a porcupine have?
faq.a: A North American porcupine has about 30,000 quills on its back, sides and tail. They are modified hairs made of keratin, hollow inside so they are light but stiff.
asks: What are porcupine quills made of?

faq.q: Why are porcupine quills hard to pull out?
faq.a: Each quill tip has hundreds of microscopic barbs pointing backwards. Researchers found the barbs help the quill go in with less force and then grip the flesh, so it is hard to pull out.
asks: Why do quills hurt so much?

faq.a: No, that is a myth. The quills are loosely attached, so they stick into an attacker at a touch and pull free from the porcupine. A swing of the tail can drive them in.
asks: How do quills come out of a porcupine?

faq.q: How does a porcupine warn predators?
faq.a: It chatters its teeth, rattles or raises its quills to look bigger, and gives off a strong smell. Most predators learn to leave it alone; if not, it turns its back and swings its tail.
asks: Why do porcupines chatter their teeth?

faq.a: Yes. Lost quills are replaced by new ones growing in, just as hairs regrow. A porcupine is never without its protection for long.
asks: Do porcupines run out of quills?
Can a porcupine lose all its quills?

facts: A North American porcupine has about 30,000 quills.
A 2012 study found the microscopic backward barbs on porcupine quills reduce the force needed to go in and increase the force needed to pull out.

quiz.say: How do porcupine quills get into an attacker?
quiz.show: Quills end up in an attacker because…
quiz.why: Quills are loosely rooted, so they stay in whatever touches them.

wrong.1: Porcupines cannot shoot quills; that is a myth.
wrong.2: There is no glue; barbs make them grip.
